newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firmer in featureless trade.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended slightly firmer in thin dealings on Monday with producer selling keeping a lid on the market, traders said.
Futures stayed within their recent ranges, unable to chase up from a session peak of 941 stg on the benchmark March position.
"There was a bit of price fixing by Malaysia. That kept December under the lid. But apart from that there was nothing else," said one trader.
Helped by a firmer opening in New York, the March cocoa ended off the day's high at 937 stg a tonne, up three stg on the day. Volume was a weak 2,667 lots.

Traders considered Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders Report to be bullish as it showed a sharp decline in the net total speculative longs (including non-reportable positions) in the two weeks ending November 11 and October 29.
They calculated the net drop as 15,641 lots.
But the market took little notice of the figures while industry demand continues to be slack and a stream of cocoa is expected from West Africa.
"The CFTC figures are good, but the market is not taking notice of anything at the moment," said one trader.
Ivory Coast set reference rates to be paid to cocoa buyers and exporters on Monday, clearing the way for the 1996/97 season to get fully underway.
Details were not immediately available, but trade sources said exporters' demands had not been fully met.
On Monday's deals, the Dec/March switch saw trades at a narrower 31 stg.
Technically, March is expected to revisit its recent low of 930, while a downtrend channel in place since October suggests support may be at 922 stg.
